title: Conditioning & Classifier-Free Guidance
interviewAnswer: Conditioning provides control information such as text, labels, embeddings or structural inputs. Classifier-free guidance combines conditioned and unconditioned predictions to strengthen adherence to the condition.
why: Conditioning is how generative models become controllable rather than producing arbitrary samples.
intuition: Give the generative model extra information—text, labels, image features, edges, compressed tokens—so the denoising/flow trajectory is guided toward outputs consistent with that signal.
deepDive: Conditioning can enter by concatenation, adaptive normalization, cross-attention, added residual branches or timestep/pooled embeddings. Classifier-free guidance trains conditional and dropped-condition cases, then combines conditional/unconditional predictions at inference to strengthen adherence. Higher guidance can improve prompt/condition alignment but reduce diversity or create artifacts.
math: CFG example: ε_guided = ε_uncond + s(ε_cond - ε_uncond)
workedExample: A compressed microstructure latent can condition the decoder so generated grains follow input structure, while a Canny ControlNet condition preserves boundaries.
commonMistakes: Assuming stronger guidance always improves quality.
Using conditioning signals that leak target information during training but are unavailable at inference.
production: Validate condition availability/quality at serving time, expose guidance controls safely, and monitor whether users can induce out-of-distribution conditions.
